content.user_title: Build Next.js Frontends With Shared Guidelines
content.value_statement: Frontend teams need consistent React and Next.js patterns across pages, components, forms, and data fetching. This skill provides practical guidance for shadcn/ui, Tailwind, Supabase, routing, performance, and TypeScript.
actual_capabilities: Explains when to use Server Components, Client Components, and Server Actions in Next.js.
Provides shadcn/ui, Tailwind CSS, React Hook Form, and Zod implementation patterns.
Shows Supabase data fetching patterns for server and client components.
Documents lazy loading, Suspense boundaries, loading states, and error states.
Defines TypeScript component, prop, import, and utility type conventions.
Includes routing, file organization, and complete feature examples.
limitations: It is guidance only and does not generate a finished application by itself.
Examples favor Next.js, React, shadcn/ui, Tailwind CSS, and Supabase.
Some resource examples mention MUI and TanStack Router patterns from related stacks.
It does not audit project-specific security, accessibility, or performance results.

use_cases.title: Create Feature Pages
use_cases.description: Use the guidelines to build pages with data fetching, loading states, errors, and typed component structure.

use_cases.title: Standardize Frontend Architecture
use_cases.description: Use the conventions to align teams on folders, components, imports, forms, and data layer patterns.

use_cases.title: Guide AI Frontend Changes
use_cases.description: Give Claude, Codex, or Claude Code clear implementation rules for Next.js and React tasks.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Page
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner task for a new route.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the frontend-dev-guidelines skill to create a Next.js App Router page for a dashboard list. Include loading, error, metadata, and typed props.

prompt_templates.title: Build a Form
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate task for validated user input.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the frontend-dev-guidelines skill to design a React Hook Form with Zod validation and shadcn/ui fields. Explain the component boundaries.

prompt_templates.title: Refactor Data Fetching
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced task for existing frontend code.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the frontend-dev-guidelines skill to refactor this feature from client-side fetching to safer Server Components or TanStack Query patterns.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a Feature Module
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced architecture task for a full feature.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the frontend-dev-guidelines skill to plan a complete feature module with routes, components, API helpers, loading states, errors, and TypeScript types.

output_examples.input: Create a profile page with server data and a loading state.
output_examples.output: A concise implementation plan with route placement, data fetching choice, metadata needs, loading UI, and component responsibilities.

output_examples.input: Review a React form for consistency with the guidelines.
output_examples.output: A focused checklist covering validation, controlled fields, submit handling, error display, and reusable shadcn/ui components.

output_examples.input: Improve a slow route that loads charts and tables.
output_examples.output: Recommendations for lazy loading heavy components, placing Suspense boundaries, memoizing expensive values, and avoiding unnecessary client components.

best_practices: Use Server Components by default and add client components only for hooks, browser APIs, or events.
Keep forms typed with React Hook Form, Zod schemas, and clear validation messages.
Add loading, error, and Suspense boundaries close to the data or component that needs them.
anti_patterns: Adding use client to every component without a browser-only need.
Creating ad hoc UI instead of using the shared shadcn/ui and Tailwind patterns.
Fetching server data into client state when a Server Component or query cache fits better.

faq.question: Which projects fit this skill best?
faq.answer: It fits Next.js and React applications that use TypeScript, shadcn/ui, Tailwind CSS, and modern data fetching.

faq.question: Can I use it without Supabase?
faq.answer: Yes. The architecture and component guidance still applies, but Supabase examples need adaptation.

faq.question: Does it write production code automatically?
faq.answer: No. It supplies implementation guidance and examples for an AI assistant or developer to follow.

faq.question: Does it support Claude Code and Codex?
faq.answer: Yes. The metadata lists Claude, Codex, and Claude Code as supported tools.

faq.question: Does it include accessibility testing?
faq.answer: It includes UI structure guidance, but it does not perform automated accessibility testing.

faq.question: Why are there MUI examples in a shadcn/ui skill?
faq.answer: Some resources include broader frontend patterns from related stacks. Treat them as adaptable examples.
